cards.title: Impact of fu Variability on PTA and Dose Recommendations
cards.claim: In Monte Carlo simulations where total concentrations are back-scaled to free concentrations using a scalar fu or an independent distribution of fu, the resulting free concentration distribution often exhibits inflated variance compared to the true free distribution. This leads to a negative bias in the estimated PK/PD cutoff (critical MIC) and an overestimation of the dose required to achieve the target PTA (e.g., 90%). The bias is exacerbated when variability in fu is incorrectly added as an independent source of noise during back-calculation, rather than being properly accounted for in the joint total/free relationship.
conditions: Monte Carlo simulations where total concentrations are scaled by fu to estimate free exposure.
Comparison between scalar fu and distributed fu approaches for back-calculation.
A reference free-exposure distribution is needed to quantify bias in this source simulation. It is not a mandatory known truth for prospective PTA based on separately qualified free exposure.
required_inputs: Distribution of fu (e.g., log-normal or uniform) used for scaling.

For source-simulation replication/bias quantification: a declared reference free-exposure distribution. For prospective PTA instead: qualified direct free exposure or a justified joint total/free model and its uncertainty.
limitations: Experimental data for individual fu distributions are rare; often based on pooled samples.
The study uses simulated data; real-world impact depends on actual binding variability of the specific drug.
The bias direction and magnitude are specific to the simulation assumptions regarding the independence or correlation of fu and total concentration errors.
cards.downstream_use: Prefer qualified direct free-concentration data when available. If only total concentrations and binding information exist, state the scalar-fu approximation and its limitations, or model the joint free/total/binding relation with justified covariance; do not add arbitrary independent fu variability during back-calculation as this increases bias in PTA estimates.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
